speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing fatigue, flank pain, and fever following recent antibiotic treatment for acute sinusitis. To help me assess your condition, can you describe the severity and location of your flank pain, and have you noticed any changes in your urine, such as frequency, urgency, or blood?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling tired, feverish, and I have flank pain. These symptoms continued even after my sinus symptoms improved.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any pain or burning when you urinate, or have you noticed any changes in the color or clarity of your urine? I also need to know if you are experiencing any nausea, vomiting, or lower back pain.

speaker: Patient
text: I was first treated with amoxicillin for sinusitis and developed a rash. Then the antibiotic was changed to cephalexin for another week, and the rash went away.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you experience any pain or burning when urinating, or notice changes in urine color or clarity? Also, are you currently experiencing any nausea, vomiting, or lower back pain?

speaker: Patient
text: I do not have nausea, vomiting, or burning with urination. I also have not noticed a major change in urine color.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of antibiotic use followed by a rash and now fever with flank pain, I am concerned about acute interstitial nephritis. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis_and_Urine_Culture

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Urinalysis shows leukocyturia present. Bacterial culture is negative. Cytospin stained with Hansel’s solution reveals 3% binucleated cells with eosinophilic, granular cytoplasm.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of eosinophils in the urine, combined with your history of antibiotic use and subsequent rash, strongly points to acute interstitial nephritis. I will now request images to further evaluate kidney involvement and confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: The sinus symptoms improved, but the flank pain and fever stayed. The rash happened during the antibiotics and then resolved after the change in medication.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of fever, flank pain, rash, and eosinophiluria following antibiotic exposure is classic for acute interstitial nephritis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Interstitial Nephritis
